analysis.title: Time For Policy To Reflect The Economy That's Here, Not The Cycle Hoped For
key_insights: October CPI and employment show the cyclical upturn in base inflation is underway. The author says markets, the Administration and Fed Chair Warsh should stop pricing expansion with falling inflation.

Employment is accelerating, following profits. Inflation follows employment with a lag, typically one year and closer to 9 months in this cycle. The 25,000 monthly payroll pace is no longer the 'new normal'.
Equity volatility to date reflects repricing of forward P/E, not a crash. The larger concern is how the FOMC reacts if equity weakness is sustained.
The Fed skipped a hike in October even though the author's Taylor Rule inputs called for one. The rule implies policy 100BP higher based on core PCE and 50BP higher based on core CPI.
Loans and deposits are growing faster than final sales of domestic product. The author expects sales to follow, which would add inflationary pressure.
The CPI diffusion index (share of categories where 3M % change exceeds 12M % change) is up to 50%, so inflation is broadening.

The market priced a 25BP-per-quarter pace ending mid-2027 and dismissed a December catch-up. After Waller and October CPI, the market prices a 12% chance of a 50BP hike in December. The author expects that to rise by month-end.
The author thinks the market underprices a 50BP hike in December and expects the Fed to lag on policy well into 2027.

The author doubts a near-term AI productivity payoff outside a few industries (entertainment, software, accountancy, law, finance, consultancy). He says those are small relative to total employment and tiny in terms of CPI impact.
The late-90s analogue cited by Warsh and Bessent does not fit. Today lacks a budget heading to surplus and a trade deficit importing disinflation at an accelerating pace.

macro_indicators.indicator: Fed funds futures: 50BP hike probability, December FOMC
macro_indicators.interpretation: Market-implied odds rose after Waller and October CPI. The author calls this cheap and expects it to rise.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The author's own estimate, which says policy is too loose and the Fed skipped a rule-implied hike in October.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The author's own estimate, a smaller gap than the core PCE version.
Half of CPI categories show 3M change above 12M change, which means inflation is broadening.

macro_indicators.indicator: FOMC hike path priced by market
macro_indicators.interpretation: The author says this path was the market's belief after the October skip, and he thinks it understates what is needed.

trade_ideas.description: Long the December 50BP FOMC hike probability (market priced at 12%)
trade_ideas.rationale: The market priced below-100% odds of a 25BP hike, which left the 50BP outcome with no value. After the CPI and Waller repricing the author still calls it cheap.
trade_ideas.risk: Sustained equity weakness could change the outlook and the Fed's reaction.

risk_factors: Sustained equity weakness could change the outlook.
A quick reversal of the tightening path if equities fall would repeat the 'original sin' that helped turn the 1960s into the 1970s.
Firms may raise prices to cover a higher wage bill that productivity and outsourcing cannot offset.
The Fed may keep lagging on policy well into 2027.
charts_described: Chart 1 plots all loans and leases, deposits and final sales of domestic product from Dec 2024 to Sep 2026, with loan growth above nominal economy growth.
Chart 2 plots the CPI diffusion index (one-month, three-month and 12-month) from Jan 2018 to Jan 2026.
Chart 3 plots goods ex food and energy, services ex rent and core CPI against private sector payrolls with a 9-month lag.
Chart 4 plots Atlanta Fed Wage Tracker growth for switch-stay, job stayer and job switcher from Jan 2023 to Sep 2026.
vol_and_positioning: Equity volatility to date is described as repricing of forward P/E, not a crash.
Equity insurance (hedging) is described as no longer as cheap as it was.
The market probability of a 50BP December hike is described as cheap relative to the author's view.
geopolitical: Tariffs and war-related oil price hikes are described as noise in prices that will fade, exposing the base inflation upturn.

tension_points.bull_case: The author argues that hotter CPI, accelerating employment and loan growth justify a 50BP December hike, which the market prices at only 12%.
tension_points.bear_case: The market expects a 25BP-per-quarter pace and the author fears the Fed will lag. Sustained equity weakness could lead the Fed to reverse the tightening path.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Sustained equity market weakness that prompts the Fed to hook the tightening trajectory.

theme_stances.key_argument: The market underprices a 50BP December hike because inflation is cyclically turning up and the Fed skipped a rule-implied hike in October.
theme_stances.evidence: Market probability of 50BP is still cheap

theme_stances.key_argument: Inflation follows the upturn in employment, with varying lags, typically a year, but closer to 9 months in this cycle.
